questions.question: What does the accounting equation A = O + L express?
options: Assets are always worth more than liabilities
Everything the business owns was funded by the owner or by outsiders
Profit equals income minus expenses
The bank balance must equal capital

questions.question: On which side does an ASSET account increase?
options: The credit side
Whichever side has more room
The debit side
Assets do not increase; only equity does

questions.question: The double-entry principle requires that every transaction:
options: Is recorded twice in the same account for safety
Affects at least two accounts, with total debits equal to total credits
Is entered in both the journal and the statements on the same day
Increases one account and leaves all others unchanged

subtopics.title: Transactions (a) and (b) — Capital and a Cash Asset Swap

questions.question: The owner deposits R100 000 as capital. What is the double entry?
options: Debit Capital R100 000; credit Bank R100 000
Debit Bank R100 000; credit Capital R100 000
Debit Bank R100 000; credit Loan R100 000
Debit Equipment R100 000; credit Bank R100 000

questions.question: Equipment is bought for R30 000 cash. What is the net effect on the accounting equation?
options: A increases by R30 000; O increases by R30 000
A decreases by R30 000; L decreases by R30 000
No net effect on A — one asset increased and another decreased by R30 000
O decreases by R30 000; L increases by R30 000

questions.question: A learner says: 'The equipment purchase had no effect on the equation, so no entries are needed.' Why is this wrong?
options: The equation actually changed by R30 000
Two entries are still required — debit Equipment, credit Bank — even though they cancel in the equation
Only one entry is needed when assets swap
Equipment purchases are recorded only at year end

questions.question: Trading stock is bought on credit for R12 000. The double entry is:
options: Debit Trading Stock R12 000; credit Creditors Control R12 000
Debit Creditors Control R12 000; credit Trading Stock R12 000
Debit Trading Stock R12 000; credit Bank R12 000
Debit Purchases R12 000; credit Capital R12 000

questions.question: Why is Creditors Control CREDITED when stock is bought on credit?
options: Because creditors are an asset that increased
Because liabilities increase on the credit side, and the business now owes more
Because all purchases are credited
Because the equation must always decrease on the right

questions.question: The business pays a creditor R5 000. The effect on the equation is:
options: A up R5 000; L up R5 000
A down R5 000; O down R5 000
A down R5 000; L down R5 000
No effect at all

questions.question: In the payment to the creditor, which account is DEBITED?
options: Bank, because money left it
Creditors Control, because the liability decreased
Trading Stock, because it was bought earlier
Capital, because the owner authorised it

questions.question: After all four transactions, total assets are R107 000 and liabilities are R7 000. For the equation to balance, owner's equity must be:
Where do incomes and expenses fit into A = O + L?
options: They form a separate fourth element of the equation
They are movements in owner's equity — income increases O, expenses decrease O
They are recorded as liabilities until year end
They only affect assets

questions.question: Wages of R2 000 are paid. The correct analysis is:
options: Debit Bank; credit Wages; O increases
Debit Wages; credit Bank; O decreases by R2 000 and A decreases by R2 000
Debit Wages; credit Capital; no equation effect
Debit Bank; credit Capital; A increases
